newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds ended easier across the board, weighed down by profit-taking, technical factors, selling pressure in government bonds and big supplies in the grey market, dealers said.

One trader said he was surprised the market was not firmer given support for the short end from the Swiss franc and three-month Eurofranc futures. But after opening firmer Conf futures slipped in line with German futures and U.S. long bonds.
Selling in long-end Swiss government bonds also undermined sentiment, but bonds held up better than futures, which turned lower after failing to break resistance at 122.
They noted pressure from big grey-market supplies, especially in KFW's 700 million franc 10-year 3.5 percent bond.
The 3-1/4 percent Newfoundland bond due in 2002 held up better, while investors sought Canadian bonds given provinces' progress in improving public finances, dealers said.
Two-year swaps sank two basis points to 1.86/1.96 percent. Five-year swaps were up two bp to 2.74/2.84, while 10-year rates rose five bp to 3.67/3.77.
Comi medium-term bond down two at 113.68
Euro Swiss francs up seven at 98.57.
